text: divMetrics provides functions calculating range diversity measures continuous attributes visualizing . package enables researchers explore divergences diversity measures select one matches research questions theoretical framework. continuous attributes, offers directly interpretable spread metrics (e.g., Gini Mean Difference). Rao’s quadratic entropy available general distance‑matrix form categorical attributes.

title: Computation and Visual Exploration of Diversity Indices
text: can install development version divMetrics GitHub :
code: # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("lukaswallrich/divMetrics")

title: Computation and Visual Exploration of Diversity Indices
text: Diversity can conceptualized different ways (Harrison & Klein, 2007): Variety: Even spread across categories represented Separation: Differences position along continuum (e.g., dispersion) Disparity: Inequality continuous attributes (e.g., age, tenure), different metrics capture different aspects diversity. divMetrics implements several key measures: CEI captures coverage theoretical range together within‑range evenness.

title: Computation and Visual Exploration of Diversity Indices
text: Calculate diversity single group:
code: library(divMetrics)  # Example: Age diversity in a team ages <- c(25, 28, 32, 45, 52)  # Standard deviation (separation) compute_sd(ages) #> [1] 11.58879  # Coefficient of variation (disparity) compute_cv(ages) #> [1] 0.3183733  # Blau's index (requires binning) compute_Blau(ages, bin_width = 10) #> [1] 0.72  # Coverage and Evenness Index compute_CEI(ages, range = c(20, 65)) #> [1] 0.4833333  # Gini Mean Difference (continuous) compute_GMD(ages) #> [1] 14.2

title: Computation and Visual Exploration of Diversity Indices
text: Compare diversity across multiple teams:
code: # Two teams with different age distributions ages <- c(25, 28, 32, 45, 52, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34) teams <- c(rep("Team A", 5), rep("Team B", 5))  # Calculate CV for each team compute_cv(ages, group = teams) #>     Team A     Team B  #> 0.31837329 0.04941059  # Calculate Blau's index for each team compute_Blau(ages, group = teams, bin_width = 10) #> Team A Team B  #>   0.72   0.00  # Get results as a data frame compute_Blau(ages, group = teams, bin_width = 10, return_df = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   group  group_members      index_value #>   <chr>  <chr>                    <dbl> #> 1 Team A 25, 28, 32, 45, 52        0.72 #> 2 Team B 30, 31, 32, 33, 34        0

title: Computation and Visual Exploration of Diversity Indices
code: # Suppose categories A/B with a distance of 2 between them D <- matrix(c(0, 2,               2, 0), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE,             dimnames = list(c("A","B"), c("A","B"))) cats <- c("A","A","B","B","A") compute_Rao(cats, D = D) #> [1] 0.96

title: Computation and Visual Exploration of Diversity Indices
code: # For continuous attributes, include CV, SD, GMD, CEI, # and (optionally) Blau if you pass bins/bin_width compute_all_metrics(ages, method = "continuous", bin_width = 10, return_df = TRUE) #> Using observed range for CEI. Specify 'range' for theoretical range. #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>      CV    SD   GMD  Blau   CEI #>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 0.238  8.13  8.62  0.58 0.646

title: Computation and Visual Exploration of Diversity Indices
text: Different metrics emphasize different aspects diversity: SD: Prioritises separation subgroups, maximised values cluster extremes CV: Focuses disparity, maximised values skewed towards lower end distribution GMD: Mean absolute difference attribute (interpretable original units) Blau’s Index: Captures categorical variety (depends binning choice) CEI: Combines range coverage evenness distribution Rao’s Index (categorical): Expected dissimilarity p’ D p using supplied distance matrix See vignette("metrics_comparison") detailed comparisons guidance.
